item.title: Marvelous Moths Program (Swannanoa) — Mon Aug 17, 7:30 PM
item.description: Join Swannanoa Valley Wild alongside Naturalist and Photographer, Sharon Mammoser, for a unique opportunity to learn and SEE some Marvelous MOTHS. Prepare to be surprised! We’ll start off in the classroom as we observe and learn about moths that live in WNC through photography and stories. Many moths are just as colorful as their day-flying cousins, the butterflies. Take the gorgeous pink and yellow rosy maple moth for example, or the yellow io moth with its shocking false eyes on its hind wings. You’ll discover why we should care about moths, how many species exist, what special adaptations they have to avoid predators and how they’re able to thrive in the dark. As darkness arrives, we will head outside to the edge of the woods, where several mothing stations will be set up consisting of a light source directed onto a white sheet. Moths, and other insects are attracted to the lights. This program is a fabulous opportunity to look closely, and photograph these marvelous creatures. We

item.title: Dialed In: A Tech Workshop — Tue Aug 18, 8:00 AM — American Underground
item.description:
Are You DIALED IN? A hands-on tech workshop presented by CreateHER Fest × Vonage DIALED IN is a five-city workshop roadshow bringing creators, developers, artists, founders, and emerging technologists together to learn to use Vonage’s VOice API and redefine communication. At this stop, Vonage Developer Advocate Dwayne Hemmings will lead a live, hands-on workshop showing how voice, video, and real-time communication can power immersive experiences in the browser. You will follow along, experiment with Vonage APIs, and see a working WebXR experience take shape in real time. What the evening includes → A community mixer with local technologists and creatives building across technology, design, art, and emerging media → A hands-on WebXR workshop led by Dwayne Hemmings → A live immersive experience and technical demo → Food, swag, and meaningful connections across the local tech ecosystem
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Mobile Health Assessment — Thu Aug 20, 9:30 AM — None
item.description:
Health Assessment is a free, confidential health screening provided through Duke benefits. It includes total cholesterol, blood pressure, blood glucose, BMI, waist circumference height, weight and body mass index measurements. Additionally, there is a goal setting and referral session with a nurse, dietitian, or fitness specialist. Many participants find the coaching session helps them get started making lifestyle changes and connects them to LIVE FOR LIFE and community resources to support them. Health Assessments are available to all active Duke employees.
Source: Duke University

item.description:

The 15-minute Zoom sessions will combine movement, breathwork, visualization and intention to create a moving meditation practice that enhances relaxation and improves well-being. item.title: Duke Farmers Market — Thu Aug 20, 11:00 AM — None
item.description:
Join us for the Duke Farmers Market! Here you can:
Find farm fresh fruits, vegetables, and other local goods at a convenient location. Enjoy a relaxed atmosphere while learning about local food systems and how eating sustainably can positively impact your health. Support local farmers and independently-owned businesses, including community partners like Duke Campus Farm.
The Duke Farmers Market is an annual market sponsored by LIVE FOR LIFE. LIVE FOR LIFE, Duke's employee wellness program, offers a variety of programs and services, such as health assessments, smoking cessation programs, fitness activities, and health education to help eligible faculty, staff and family members reach health and fitness goals.

item.title: THE LONG EXHALE | A GROUP EXHIBITION — Thu Aug 20, 5:00 PM — 5 Points Gallery
item.description:
5 Points Gallery is pleased to present The Long Exhale, bringing together work by the ten artists of 5 Points Gallery. As the pace of summer begins to soften, The Long Exhale invites visitors to pause, look closely, and linger. The exhibition offers a refreshing mix of painting, sculpture, fused glass, mixed media, and finely crafted furniture, with each artist offering a distinct creative perspective. Join us for the Opening Reception on Friday, August 21, 2026, from 6–9 pm to meet the artists. The exhibition runs from August 20 through September 12, 2026. Visit 5 Points Gallery in person or online at https://5pointsgallery.com. All work from the exhibition is available for shipping or pickup. Gallery hours: Thursdays and Fridays 5–9pm and Saturdays 1–9pm. Artists are available to talk about their work. For a private viewing, contact us at info@5pointsgallery.com.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Moth Night at TAG (Charlotte) — Fri Aug 28, 8:30 PM
item.description:
Join the North Carolina Wildlife Federation Charlotte Wildlife Stewards and City of Charlotte Landscape Management for an exciting night of mothing, led by City Arborist and entomologist Laurie Reid. As the sun goes down, we will have lights and sheets set up to attract our native moths, and you’re certain to see some moths you’ve never seen before. Not only are moths great pollinators, but they are also an important food source for our breeding birds! In addition to moths, we will likely see other species of nocturnal wildlife too! It’s fantastic fun for all ages! Download the iNaturalist app to help you identify the moths and contribute to the National Moth Week Bioblitz. This exploration is a fun way to learn about the “night crew!” REGISTER HERE
Source: NC Wildlife Federation

item.title: Threads of the Past at Historic Fort Defiance — Sat Aug 29, 12:00 PM — Fort Defiance
item.description:
For one day only, step back into the 19th century as historic textiles take center stage at the home of Major General William Lenoir. Explore what life was like on the frontier through the clothing, quilts, and other textiles used by the people who lived here. Costumed docents will bring these fascinating stories to life on a special tour that offers a rare glimpse into the everyday lives of generations past.
Authentic textiles will be on display by guided tour of the home. Admission to the house is $7/adults and $5/children ages 6-14 years old. All proceeds go to Fort Defiance's continued operations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Sat Nov 14 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.

On select days this summer, the cabins will come alive with the sights, sounds, and smells of 18th-century life in the North Carolina mountains.
From open-hearth cooking and blacksmithing to weaving, spinning, woodworking, and frontier chores, guests will experience a day in the life of the early settlers who called this region home. Our interpreters and volunteers will demonstrate traditional skills throughout the village, inviting you to explore, ask questions, and connect with the everyday stories of Appalachian history.
